tasks.title: Lecture #46
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an architecture class.
tasks.transcript:
Man: Have you ever thought about how ancient concrete structures like Roman amphitheatres and aqueducts have managed to last for thousands of years, while modern concrete buildings seem to fall apart and need replacing after just a few decades? For a long time, researchers thought the secret to Roman concrete's durability was volcanic ash. That makes sense, since volcanic ash was a major ingredient, and it was explicitly described as such by architects and historians who were writing at the time.
But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate. These formed because the Romans used dry, quick lime in their mix instead of the way we make concrete today called Portland cement, where lime gets mixed with water first, then blended with everything else. When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water gets in, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks. So the concrete basically heals itself, fixes the cracks, and gets stronger over time.
Funny thing is, researchers have noticed these chunks in Roman concrete for ages, but they just figured they were a production flaw, like someone didn't mix the ingredients well enough. Anyway, considering how short lived modern concrete is,and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might be able to use some of these ancient Roman tricks in future construction.

questions.stem: What is the main focus of the talk?

options.A: Restoring ancient structures using modern materials
options.B: A building material used by the ancient Romans
options.C: New research on the design of Roman amphitheaters
options.D: The ancient origins of a modern construction method

questions.analysis: 答案: B 题目问的是: 这篇讲座的主要焦点是什么？ 定位原文: "Have you ever thought about how ancient concrete structures... managed to last for thousands of years... But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate." 选项分析: A. Restoring ancient structures using modern materials (使用现代材料修复古建筑) - 错误。讲座讨论的是古罗马材料本身的特性，而非修复技术。 B. A building material used by the ancient Romans (古罗马人使用的一种建筑材料) - 正确。整篇讲座都在分析古罗马混凝土（Roman concrete）为何如此耐用。 C. New research on the design of Roman amphitheaters (关于罗马圆形竞技场设计的新研究) - 错误。圆形竞技场只是作为耐久混凝土的例子被提及，并非研究焦点。 D. The ancient origins of a modern construction method (一种现代建筑方法的古代起源) -错误。讲座对比了古代和现代（Portland cement）的不同，重点在于古代材料的优越性，而非现代方法源于古代。

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about volcanic ash?

options.A: It provides evidence that volcanoes damaged Roman buildings.
options.B: Its presence in Roman buildings was discovered only in recent decades.
options.C: It is less important for the durability of ancient Roman buildings than researchers used to believe.
options.D: Its use may lead to improvements in modern building techniques.

questions.analysis: 答案: C 题目问的是: 说话者暗示了关于火山灰的什么信息？ 定位原文: "For a long time, researchers thought the secret to Roman concrete's durability was volcanic ash... But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate." 选项分析: A. It provides evidence that volcanoes damaged Roman buildings. (它提供了火山损坏罗马建筑的证据。) - 错误。文中未提及。 B. Its presence in Roman buildings was discovered only in recent decades. (它在罗马建筑中的存在是近几十年才发现的。) - 错误。文中说它一直是主要成分，且被古代历史学家 描述过。 C. It is less important for the durability of ancient Roman buildings than researchers used to believe. (对于古罗马建筑的耐久性来说，它不如研究人员过去认为的那么重要。) - 正确。说话者指出研究人员“曾经认为”秘密是火山灰，但“结果发现”真正的秘密是碳酸钙，暗示火山灰的重要性被高估了。 D. Its use may lead to improvements in modern building techniques. (它的使用可能会导致现代建筑技术的改进。) - 错误。文中提到改进现代技术是依靠“Roman tricks”（即碳酸钙/生石灰技术），而非火山灰。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about chunks of calcium carbonate in concrete?

options.A: They result from not enough mixing.
options.B: They enable concrete to repair itself.
options.C: They can cause concrete to crack.

questions.analysis: 答案: B 题目问的是: 说话者关于混凝土中的碳酸钙块说了什么？ 定位原文: "When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water gets in, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks. So the concrete basically heals itself..." 选项分析: A. They result from not enough mixing. (它们是由于搅拌不充分造成的。) - 错误。这是研究人员“曾经以为”的（production flaw），但被说话者否定了。 B. They enable concrete to repair itself. (它们使混凝土能够自我修复。) - 正确。文中明确提到“heals itself”和“seal up the cracks”。 C. They can cause concrete to crack. (它们会导致混凝土开裂。) - 错误。它们是修复裂缝的，不是导致裂缝的。 D. They cannot react with water. (它们不能与水反应。) - 错误。文中说它们“react with the water”。

questions.stem: What is the speaker's attitude toward modern concrete?

options.A: He is impressed by the complex methods of producing it.
options.B: He is excited about a new way of producing large amounts of it quickly.
options.C: He believes that it was originally inspired by the ancient Romans.
options.D: He thinks that it needs major improvement.

questions.analysis: 答案: D 题目问的是: 说话者对现代混凝土的态度是什么？ 定位原文: "...considering how short lived modern concrete is, and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might be able to use some of these ancient Roman tricks..." 选项分析: A. He is impressed by the complex methods of producing it. (他对生产它的复杂方法印象深刻。) - 错误。文中未提及对方法的赞赏。 B. He is excited about a new way of producing large amounts of it quickly. (他对一种快速大量生产它的新方法感到兴奋。) - 错误。文中未提及。 C. He believes that it was originally inspired by the ancient Romans. (他认为它最初是受古罗马人启发。) - 错误。文中未提及灵感来源。 D. He thinks that it needs major improvement. (他认为它需要重大改进。) - 正确。说话者指出现代混凝土“short lived”（寿命短）且“bad for the environment”（对环境有害），并认为借鉴古罗马技术是“exciting”（令人兴奋的），暗示现代混凝土存在缺陷，急需改进。
